discovery: Discovery of geometric and topological phases in quantum mechanics (Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University, Israel, and Chapman University, USA

subfield: Quantum physics / condensed matter theory (geometric and topological phases)
motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm) showed in 1959 that electromagnetic potentials act on quantum particles even where fields vanish, a prediction confirmed by Tonomura's electron holography and ubiquitous in mesoscopic rings, where Aharonov-Bohm oscillations probe electron coherence. In 1984 Berry discovered the general geometric phase acquired under adiabatic cyclic evolution, revealing the Aharonov-Bohm phase as one instance of a universal holonomy. Together these insights created the language of geometric phases and Berry curvature, which underlies the modern understanding of the quantum Hall effect, anomalous Hall and valley transport in graphene, topological insulators and superconductors, polarization theory, and topological photonic and cold-atom systems. Few theoretical ideas have unified so many disparate phenomena and been so thoroughly verified experimentally. Berry's semiclassical work on quantum chaos further enriches this legacy. The discovery is foundational for the second quantum revolution.
